prompt: Split-year treatment allows a tax year to be divided into which two parts for an eligible UK resident?
option_a: UK part taxable and overseas part not taxable
option_b: UK part not taxable and overseas part taxable
option_c: Only employment income taxable in both parts
option_d: Both parts fully taxable in UK
explanation: Your notes state the year can be split into a UK part (taxable) and an overseas part (not taxable).

prompt: Which is one of the listed leaving-UK split-year scenarios?
option_a: Moving overseas to retire with no other conditions
option_b: Leaving UK to begin full-time work overseas
option_c: Leaving UK for part-time overseas work only
option_d: Leaving UK for a temporary holiday abroad
explanation: A listed leaving case is departure to begin full-time work overseas.

prompt: Which spouse-related event can support leaving-UK split-year treatment under your notes?
option_a: Accompanying spouse to begin full-time work overseas
option_b: Accompanying spouse on short-term study overseas
option_d: Accompanying spouse while remaining UK-home based
explanation: Your notes include accompanying a spouse who starts full-time work overseas.

prompt: In the “to live abroad” leaving case, which combination is described?
option_a: Keep UK house, spend substantial UK time, no overseas ties
option_b: Sell UK house, keep significant UK time, no foreign ties
option_c: Sell UK house, minimal UK time, establish ties with another country
option_d: Retain UK house and increase UK workdays
explanation: The notes specify living abroad with sale of UK house, minimal UK time, and ties with another country.

prompt: Which coming-to-UK scenario is listed for split-year treatment?
option_a: Acquires UK home and had sufficient ties before acquiring it
option_b: Acquires UK home and did not have sufficient ties to be UK resident before acquiring it
option_c: Acquires UK home and automatically becomes UK resident from prior year
option_d: Acquires UK home while remaining fully overseas resident indefinitely
explanation: One listed case is acquiring a UK home with no sufficient UK-residence ties beforehand.

prompt: For a coming-to-UK work case in your notes, what duration is required?
option_a: Full-time work in UK for at least 6 months
option_b: Full-time work in UK for at least 9 months
option_c: Full-time work in UK for at least 1 year
option_d: Any UK work with no minimum duration
explanation: The notes specify full-time work in the UK for at least a year, with no sufficient ties before.

prompt: Which returning-to-UK split-year scenario is listed?
option_a: Returns after holiday abroad regardless of work history
option_b: Returns following period where they (or spouse) worked full-time overseas
option_d: Returns only if UK home was never acquired
explanation: A listed coming case is return after a period of full-time overseas work by the individual or spouse.
